column1: # Curated machine facts (WO-1.7, D109-D111): parallels, speed, EU and overclock rules of GT's
# multiblocks, read by hand from GT5-Unofficial's source at the pinned tag 5.09.54.265 (GTNH 2.9.0;
# sources jar GT5-Unofficial-5.09.54.265-sources.jar from the GTNH maven, sha256
# (numbers and rules) with the place in GT's code they come from, no GT code. GT is LGPL-3.0.
# ShadowTheAge's machines.ts (MIT, Copyright (c) 2025 ShadowTheAge) was a reference for which
# machines have special rules; no number is taken from it.
# One row per machine class (the machine pass's "class"; class@meta for one of several machines
# of a class). gos db build loads every row into machine_fact (source curated), where it wins
# over the tooltip parser's row for the same key. Columns:
#   machine      the class; name: its English name when curated (a comment, not checked)
#   processing   logic (GT's ProcessingLogic over its maps) | custom (its own recipe check) |
#                generator (burns fuel for EU or steam) | none (runs no recipes)
#   parallel     max parallel recipes; speed: duration is divided by it; eu_modifier: recipe
#                EU/t is multiplied by it; formulas over the variables in
#                core/gregtec/ingest/machine_facts.py (vt = voltage tier of the summed hatch
#                voltage, coil_tier = HeatingCoilLevel.getTier(), ...; each one says whether
#                its value comes from how the machine is built, its state while running
#                (ramp, overheated, ...) or the recipe it runs (recipe_tier, ...))
#   oc           standard | perfect | heat | heat_no_discount | limited_perfect | none | custom
#   extra        more key=value facts, ";"-separated; key[recipe map] for one map (a mode).
#                A custom machine with no recipe map (D144) also gives what one run takes:
#                duration (ticks), eu_t, consumes[fluid:<name> or registry@meta], slots,
#                output_mul, outputs (chain, drops or patterns), chain[<mode>] (the recipe
#                maps of a mode, map(classes) > map(classes) ...) and partial=outputs (the DB
#                can't give its outputs; the rest of the row stands)
#   confidence   0..1 for every fact of the row; parallels and OC rules count at >= 0.8
#   cite         gt@<tag>:<file>#<methods>;<file>#<methods>, files relative to the source root
#   note         what the variables mean here, and anything a planner must know
# A blank cell makes no claim. "n/a": the machine runs no recipes. flag=review: the planner can't
# model this machine yet (the note says why); it is listed as flagged in the build report.

column11: its own checkProcessing, no recipe map: each run takes run_parallel ores, at most parallel (getMaxInputEu() / 30, the tooltip's 'Unlimited Parallels'), and as many as the lubricant (2 L each), distilled water (200 L each) and input items pay for; any input item of a CHAIN_CLASSES class counts as an ore. 30 EU/t per ore and a fixed time per mode (getRecipeTickTime), no overclocks. mode: ProcessingMode's ordinal (screwdriver; NBT mode): 0 macerate, wash, thermal centrifuge, macerate (30 s); 1 macerate, wash, macerate, centrifuge (15 s); 2 macerate, macerate, centrifuge (10 s); 3 macerate, wash, sift (20 s); 4 macerate, chemical bath, macerate, centrifuge (17 s); 5 macerate, chemical bath, thermal centrifuge, macerate (32 s); 6 forge hammer, forge hammer, simple washer (1 s). Outputs: chain[mode] over the DB's recipes: each step looks up each stack's recipe (no voltage check; the washer with distilled water, the simple washer with water, neither used up) and multiplies its outputs by the stack size, whatever the recipe's input amount; a stack with no recipe passes on. A chance output is the ceiling of a normal approximation around n x chance (GT's random), so n x chance on average, up to one more per output and step. Only a recipe's item outputs are kept: its fluid outputs are voided (getOutputStack reads mOutputs only; the centrifuge's and chemical bath's have some). The chemical bath step pays its recipe's first fluid per item (the fluid in the hatches picks the recipe) and passes on what it can't pay for. Sneaking with the screwdriver voids stone, netherrack, endstone, marble and red granite dust

Normal mode only: GT registers no other EIG mode at this version, so IC2 crops are not taken. parallel is the seeds it holds in all, slots x 64 in any mix (addCrop caps only the total, so one seed type may take all of it; the tooltip's 'each slot holds 64 seeds' suggests otherwise); slots (from EV: 1, 2, 4, ... per tier) caps the seed types. run_parallel is the seeds planted; they stay in, not used up. No overclocks: the tier sets the time (100 / (tier - 3) ticks, at least 1 s) and the EU ((long)(V[tier] x 0.99); V[14], MAX, is 2^31 - 8, so eu_t holds to UXV). Weed-EX is needed only from 1000 seeds; short of it, up to 2% of the seeds (random) die each run. Fertilizer: bone meal, or with Forestry Forestry:fertilizerCompound@0 (the same count, any mix), at most 2 per seed; fertilizer is the count given. partial outputs: each seed type's drops come from the game, not a recipe map: the plant's getDrops at full growth (meta 7, Natura 8) at fortune 0, averaged over 1000 harvests, less the seed (a true seed's drops lose every seed); stems (melon, pumpkin) 100 harvests, flowers drop themselves, the rainbow cactus with Thaumic Bases; times output_mul.
